title: UNIT 5: MAGNETISM
notes: ✓ Magnetism → Interaction in which magnets and moving electric charges produce magnetic fields and magnetic forces.

title: 5.1 MAGNET
notes:
✓ Magnet → Material/object that produces a magnetic field and can attract magnetic materials such as iron and steel.

◆ LODESTONE
✓ Lodestone → Naturally magnetized mineral (magnetite) with magnetic properties.

◆ TYPES OF MAGNETS
✓ Permanent magnet → Retains its magnetism for a long time; e.g. steel magnets.
✓ Temporary magnet → Becomes magnetized in a magnetic field but loses most of its magnetism when the field is removed; e.g. iron nails and paper clips.
✓ Electromagnet → Coil of wire around an iron core that becomes magnetic when current flows. Its strength can be controlled by changing the current.

◆ PROPERTIES
✓ Every magnet → Has two poles: North (N) and South (S).
✓ Like poles → Repel: N–N, S–S.
✓ Unlike poles → Attract: N–S.
✓ Magnetic poles → Always occur in pairs.
✓ Cutting a magnet → Produces smaller magnets, each with N and S poles.
✓ Freely suspended magnet → Points approximately North–South.

✓ Permanent magnets → Can be weakened by heating, hammering or improper striking.

title: 5.2 MAGNETIC FIELD
notes:
✓ Magnetic field → Region around a magnet or moving electric charge where magnetic forces act.

◆ MAGNETIC FIELD (B)
✓ Magnetic field → Vector quantity.
✓ SI unit → Tesla (T).
✓ Direction at a point → Direction a north magnetic pole/compass would point.

◆ MAGNETIC FIELD LINES
✓ Magnetic field lines → Imaginary lines used to represent magnetic fields.
✓ Outside a magnet → N → S.
✓ Inside a magnet → S → N.
✓ Field lines → Form continuous closed loops.
✓ Field lines → Never cross one another.
✓ Closer lines → Stronger magnetic field.
✓ Farther apart → Weaker magnetic field.
✓ Direction of B → Tangent to the field line.

✓ FIELD STRENGTH → Greater line density means a stronger magnetic field.

title: 5.3 EARTH'S MAGNETIC FIELD & THE COMPASS
notes:
✓ Earth's magnetic field → Similar to that of a giant bar magnet.

◆ EARTH'S MAGNETIC FIELD
✓ Also called → Geomagnetic field.
✓ Main origin → Movement of molten iron in Earth's outer core.
✓ Earth's magnetic axis → Tilted about 11° relative to its geographic axis.
✓ Earth → Has geographic poles and magnetic poles.

◆ COMPASS
✓ Compass → Contains a small magnetized needle that can rotate freely.
✓ Compass needle → Aligns with Earth's magnetic field and indicates magnetic North–South directions.

◆ IMPORTANT
✓ Earth's geographic North region → Is near a magnetic south pole in the bar-magnet sense, which attracts the north-seeking end of a compass needle.

✓ Some animals → Including pigeons, bees, sea turtles and fish, can sense Earth's magnetic field and use it for orientation/navigation.

title: 5.4 MAGNETIC FIELD OF A CURRENT-CARRYING CONDUCTOR
notes:
✓ Moving electric charges → Produce magnetic fields.
✓ Current-carrying conductor → Produces a magnetic field around it.

◆ STRAIGHT CURRENT-CARRYING WIRE
✓ Magnetic field → Forms concentric circles around the wire.

◆ MAGNITUDE
B = μ₀I/(2πd)

✓ B → Magnetic field strength (T).
✓ μ₀ → Permeability of free space = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.
✓ I → Current (A).
✓ d → Perpendicular distance from the wire (m).

◆ DEPENDENCE
✓ B ∝ I → Increasing current increases B.
✓ B ∝ 1/d → Increasing distance decreases B.

◆ RIGHT-HAND RULE
✓ Right thumb → Direction of conventional current.
✓ Curled fingers → Direction of the magnetic field.

✓ KEY IDEA → A current creates a circular magnetic field around its conductor.

title: 5.5 MAGNETIC FORCE ON A MOVING CHARGE
notes:
✓ Moving charged particle → Experiences a magnetic force when it moves through a magnetic field.

◆ MAGNITUDE
F = qvB sin θ

✓ q → Magnitude of charge (C).
✓ v → Particle speed (m/s).
✓ B → Magnetic field strength (T).
✓ θ → Angle between v and B.

◆ SPECIAL CASES
✓ θ = 0° or 180° → F = 0.
✓ θ = 90° → F = qvB, maximum force.

◆ DIRECTION
✓ Magnetic force → Is perpendicular to both velocity v and magnetic field B.

◆ RIGHT-HAND RULE
✓ Positive charge → Thumb indicates velocity, fingers indicate magnetic field, and perpendicular palm direction indicates force.
✓ Negative charge → Force direction is opposite to that obtained for a positive charge.

✓ KEY IDEA → A stationary charge does not experience magnetic force from a magnetic field; the charge must be moving.

title: 5.6 MAGNETIC FORCE ON A CURRENT-CARRYING WIRE
notes:
✓ Current-carrying wire → Experiences a magnetic force when placed in an external magnetic field because its current consists of moving charges.

◆ FORCE EQUATION
F = ILB sin θ

✓ I → Current (A).
✓ L → Length of wire in the field (m).
✓ B → Magnetic field strength (T).
✓ θ → Angle between current direction and magnetic field.

◆ SPECIAL CASES
✓ θ = 0° → F = 0.
✓ θ = 90° → F = ILB, maximum force.

◆ DIRECTION
✓ Magnetic force → Is perpendicular to the plane containing the current and magnetic field.

◆ RIGHT-HAND RULE
✓ Fingers → B.
✓ Thumb → Conventional current.
✓ Palm → Direction of force.

◆ APPLICATION
✓ Electric motors and moving-coil galvanometers → Operate using magnetic force on current-carrying conductors.

title: 5.7 MAGNETIC FORCE BETWEEN TWO PARALLEL CURRENT-CARRYING WIRES
notes:
✓ Each current-carrying wire → Produces a magnetic field that acts on the other wire, producing a magnetic force between them.

◆ SAME CURRENT DIRECTION
✓ Parallel wires carrying currents in the same direction → Attract.

◆ OPPOSITE CURRENT DIRECTIONS
✓ Parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions → Repel.

◆ KEY IDEA
✓ Wire 1 → Produces magnetic field.
✓ Magnetic field of wire 1 → Exerts force on wire 2.
✓ Wire 2 → Similarly exerts an equal and opposite force on wire 1.

✓ RULE TO REMEMBER → Same direction = attraction; opposite direction = repulsion.

title: 5.8 APPLICATIONS OF MAGNETISM
notes:
✓ Magnetism → Is widely used in medicine, homes, electronics, navigation and industry.

◆ HEALTH & MEDICINE
✓ MRI machines → Use powerful magnetic fields to produce detailed images of internal body structures.
✓ Magnetic techniques → Can also be used in some cancer-treatment applications.

◆ HOME
Refrigerator magnets.
Compasses.
Electric motors in appliances.
Doorbells.
Phones and toys.

◆ COMPUTERS & ELECTRONICS
✓ Magnetic hard drives → Store data using magnetic states.
✓ Speakers → Magnets and coils convert electrical signals into sound vibrations.
✓ Magnetic strips → Used for data storage on cards.

◆ ELECTRIC POWER & INDUSTRY
✓ Generators → Magnets help convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.
✓ Motors → Magnetic forces convert electrical energy into mechanical motion.
✓ Electromagnetic cranes → Lift and transport large metal objects.
✓ Magnetic separation → Separates magnetic materials/ores.
✓ Food processing → Removes unwanted metal particles.

◆ NAVIGATION
✓ Magnetic compasses → Use Earth's magnetic field to determine direction.
